matched.location: POST /api/settings endpoint and EJS template compilation chain
matched.expectedTitle: Prototype Pollution to Remote Code Execution via Template Engine Gadget
matched.actualTitle: Prototype Pollution via Insecure JSON Deserialization - POST /api/settings + Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via EJS Prototype Pollution
matched.matchReason: The actual findings comprehensively document the complete exploit chain expected in the vulnerability: (1) /api/settings endpoint accepts user JSON without filtering __proto__ (confirmed in 'Prototype Chain Pollution' and 'Prototype Pollution via Object.__proto__' findings), (2) Object.prototype is successfully polluted with attacker-controlled properties (confirmed by /api/debug endpoint showing polluted properties), (3) EJS template engine reads polluted prototype properties specifically the outputFunctionName gadget (confirmed in 'SSTI via EJS Prototype Pollution' and 'SSTI via Prototype Pollution' findings), (4) RCE is achieved through template compilation with injected malicious code (confirmed with require('child_process').execSync() examples in multiple findings). All three actual findings (findings 2, 6, 9) collectively demonstrate the exact vulnerability chain described in the expected finding.

extra.title: Authentication Bypass on POST /api/reset - Unauthenticated Access to Admin Function
extra.assessment: New discovery - Related to the prototype pollution vulnerability but represents a separate authentication control bypass. This allows unauthenticated users to trigger state resets, which could be used to clear prototype pollution evidence or interfere with exploit attempts. While not required by the expected finding, this is a legitimate security vulnerability that increases the impact of the prototype pollution vulnerability.

extra.title: Authentication Bypass - Admin Panel and API Endpoints Accessible Without Credentials
extra.assessment: New discovery - Multiple endpoints including the vulnerable /api/settings are publicly accessible without authentication. This is a critical finding that enables easier exploitation of the prototype pollution vulnerability, as attackers don't need to authenticate to access the vulnerable endpoint. This compounds the prototype pollution risk significantly.

extra.title: Information Disclosure via Health Endpoint - Sensitive Technical Details Exposed
extra.assessment: New discovery - The /health endpoint discloses that the application uses Pug template engine (in addition to EJS identified elsewhere), cache configuration, and Express framework. This is helpful reconnaissance for targeting the prototype pollution vulnerability with specific template engine gadgets. While not directly part of the expected vulnerability, it enables more effective exploitation by confirming the exact template engines in use.

extra.title: Insecure Deserialization via Prototype Pollution on /render-new Endpoint
extra.assessment: New discovery - An additional endpoint vulnerable to prototype pollution via query parameters rather than just POST body. This represents an alternative attack surface for the same underlying prototype pollution vulnerability. The __proto__ parameter in query strings can pollute Object.prototype and affect template rendering, providing an alternate path to the same RCE goal.

extra.title: Unauthorized Access to Admin Reset Function - Missing Authentication
extra.assessment: New discovery - Duplicate/related to authentication bypass finding #3. Confirms the /api/reset endpoint lacks authentication despite being marked as an admin function. Enables attackers to reset prototype pollution state or manipulate application state without authorization.
